summary:
ORBITCARE 5X - Overview

ORBITCARE 5X – A tool for astronaut health and environment monitoring to ensure the safety of astronauts on the space missions. It brings the health details of astronauts and space environment conditions under one hood. The platform allows monitoring of vital health indicators, detection of possible environmental threats, comparison of crew conditions, and evaluation of the level of crew readiness to go on a mission. We want to help interpret the influence of space conditions on astronauts and on their mission achievement. The platform provides data analysis and visual indicators as a well-organized dashboard, which helps users to understand possible risks and make informed decisions. Such a project shows how technology, data analysis and an AI-based approach can make space missions safer and better planned.
details:
ORBITCARE 5X is a deep-space functional hazards web site for improving human health engineering decisions on long-duration crewed missions. On Moon or Mars missions, communication latency prevents real-time medical guidance from Earth ground control. Our project solves this autonomy problem by continuously monitoring all five Human Research Program (HRP) threats promulgated by NASA: 1) Space Radiation, 2) Isolation & Stress, 3) Hostile Closed Environments, 4) Altered Gravity Fields and 5) Distance From Earth.

Capabilities and how it works.

Automatically executes a 7-step health process (Ingest, Sanitize, Personalize, Detect, Score, Fuse, and Alert) on spacecraft telemetry. The engine generates 0-100 hazard sub-scores and then an A+ to F Total Mission Grade so astronauts are not overwhelmed by thousands of complex sensor numbers.How it's Creative:

Cross-Hazard Fusion is our main creative differentiator. Hazard scores can get to dangerously low levels before averaging becomes apparent. To counter, we created two key safety rules:

The Bottleneck Rule: Should any single hazard drop to critical danger (RED score<35), the overall mission grade is immediately capped at Grade D. A single risk failure is never obscured by better scores of other risks.

The Compounding Penalty: A 10 point risk score penalty is applied when three or more hazards reach the warning state (Score between 50-65) at the same time.

Benefits and Intended Impact:

The platform aims to reduce mission aborts due to cognitive overload by crew members through a HUD for crewmembers that shows vital signs, sparklines for crewmember engagement, an interactive Mission Simulator to assist in contingency planning, and real-time alerts for potentially mission-critical space weather events. The intended impact of the platform is to help crewmembers take timely preventative measures to mitigate the risks of space weather to prevent the situation from deteriorating to a medical emergency.

Technologies :

Python. FastAPI, SQLite, SQLAlchemy, NumPy, Pandas Backend. Front end: HTML5, CSS3, Modern JavaScript (ES Modules). Visualisation via Chart.js. Quality assurance with 36 automated tests.

Considerations :

Scientific integrity and patient safety were our focus. All vital signs were clearly marked as SIMULATED. Grades were simply used as an early warning triage tool. Were not meant as a medical diagnostic. We also added alerting to reduce duplicate alerts and offline caching to handle times when there was no communication, with the spacecraft.
